transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-04-21 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/rec/ff-20260421-mistralgrove

Summary:
Quick kickoff/immersion for Mistral Grove's implementation with focus on access, network intake (VPC), security checklist, and initial perf expectations for a short pilot. AE+SE+CSM from Redwood; SRE, CTO, Product, Security on the customer side. Several follow-ups agreed (runbook, perf script, VPC peering).

Topics:
- Access & accounts (SSO/SAML, RBAC)
- Network/VPC peering and IP ranges
- Pilot scope & success criteria (latency, cost, quality)
- Security/compliance (KMS, audit logs, SOC2)
- Early performance benchmarking and runbook

Transcript body:
00:00 Avery (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off in a sec, appreciate you making time, i'm avery chen, i'll be your AE on the engagement.
00:10 Michael (CTO): hey thanks avery, michael here, glad to get this moving, we've got priya and tomás and ellen on the call too.
00:18 Priya (SRE): hi all, priya from infra, main thing for us is network and perf — we want to validate latency at 99p and avoid noisy neighbor issues.
00:30 Samir (Redwood SE): great, quick intro — i'm samir, i'll own the technical intake and the perf validation. i can walk through our benchmark script and the expected telemetry we'll need.
00:40 Tomás (PM): i'm tomás, i'll be owning success criteria and prompt sets for the eval.
00:48 Lena (CSM): lena from success, i'll be running the onboarding timeline and checklists.
00:55 Avery: high level agenda — 1) access & onboarding steps, 2) network/VPC intake, 3) pilot success criteria, 4) security questions and 5) next steps.
01:05 Michael: sounds good. for access we want SSO and least privilege, plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM — how does that work today?
01:20 Samir: we support SAML/SSO and can map groups to RBAC. audit logs are available via the Console API or forwarded to a cloud logging endpoint — note: our console sometimes shows as 'Redwood Consol' in older docs, but it's the same thing.
01:36 Ellen (Security): on KMS — we need to know if you support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and what the key rotation looks like. also data residency for logs.
01:48 Samir: yes, we have KMS integrations; for private/on-prem installs we can integrate to customer KMS or HSM. rotation is your KMS policy; we just call the envelope keys. i'll share the integration notes.
01:58 Priya: on networking — we run in a locked-down VPC. how do peering or private endpoints work? we need IP ranges and a test plan.
02:10 Samir: for Dedicated/Private we'll talk through VPC peering and private endpoints. i'll need your VPC CIDRs and a list of egress IPs. we can set up a short window to run perf tests from your prod-like environment.
02:25 Tomás: for the pilot we want to test 10k requests/day initially, prioritize a 300ms p99 target for short prompts, and measure cost per 1k tokens. also want to validate fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
02:45 Samir: that helps. note: latency depends on batching and KV cache warmness — if your request patterns have long common prefixes we can cache prefixes to reduce cost and latency. also quantization profiles may change throughput; we'll recommend profiles after we see the eval prompts.
03:05 Priya: what's the ramp plan for traffic? we prefer a staged rollout with canary and then 10/50/100% ramp. can the platform do canaries?
03:20 Avery: yes — rollouts are supported for canary/A-B and auto-fallback rules. we'll document recommended ramp increments in the runbook.
03:28 Michael: security paperwork — we need SOC2 documentation and an audit contact. do you have an SOC2 report we can share?
03:38 Lena: yes, i'll attach the latest SOC2 and ISO summary in the follow-up email. we also have a security appendix that covers KMS, RBAC, retention policies.
03:48 Ellen: also need to confirm retention periods for logs and prompts, plus whether embeddings are stored and how long.
03:58 Samir: embeddings by default are ephemeral for the hosted product; for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention per customer. i'll add a note about default retention values.
04:08 Tomás: on the eval prompts — we'll send a set of 30 canonical prompts that represent our user flows. can we pin a model version for the pilot?
04:20 Samir: yes, you can pin model versions and we'll snapshot them for the duration of the eval. if we need to fallback to a smaller model we can set an automatic fallback policy.
04:32 Priya: for perf tests, what telemetry do you expose so we can correlate with our APM?
04:40 Samir: we export per-request latency, token counts, model id, route, and a trace id you can stitch in your APM. we'll share a tracing hook and sample span mappings.
04:55 Michael: do you support private deployment (on-prem) or are we looking at Dedicated reserved capacity first?
05:05 Avery: for this engagement we recommended starting with Dedicated reserved capacity to get predictable throughput; on-prem is possible but typically later. we can scope both if you like.
05:18 Ellen: one concern — vendor lock in and off-ramps. if we go Dedicated and keep data on your platform, what's the export process?
05:30 Lena: we provide export tooling and migration playbooks; we'll include that in the runbook for clarity.
05:38 Tomás: timelines — we want a pilot within 3 weeks if possible. is that realistic?
05:46 Samir: 3 weeks is doable if we get access and VPC details this week and the prompt set by Friday. perf runs we can do in the second week.
05:56 Priya: ok i'll make time for the network intake next week.
06:03 Avery: perfect. quick note — i might send a short checklist with items for SSO, IP ranges, service account, and contacts.
06:12 Michael: that'd be great. also send cost model examples so finance can eyeball the 1k token cost estimates.
06:22 Avery: will do.
06:28 Lena: i'll create the weekly cadence and invite the core team.
06:33 Samir: i'll drop the perf script and an example run. please beware transcription nuance, some product terms may appear in the automatic transcript as 'K V cash' or similar, ignore that.
06:45 Ellen: thanks.
06:50 Avery: recap of next steps — redwood sends runbook + SOC2 + perf script; customer shares prompt set + VPC diagram + IP ranges; schedule VPC intake; set weekly check-in.
07:05 Michael: agreed. thanks all.
